title: The Dashboard Clock Is Two Minutes Fast
premise: At a parked stop, a traveler compares the dashboard clock with a wristwatch and finds the dashboard two minutes ahead. They repeat the comparison later without resetting anything, so the only result is that both clocks remain readable.

title: The Calendar Page Is Still on Last Month
premise: A small paper calendar is opened to a page whose final date has already passed. The traveler flips it forward, then turns back to check that the old page really was old.

title: We Watch the Minute Change to 42
premise: The camera holds on a parked dashboard clock at 41 and waits for the display to change. It does, and the next shot gives 42 the same amount of attention.

title: The Daily Chart Has a Blank Row at 11:00
premise: A traveler's daily chart has one empty line beside 11:00, and the camera returns to it at the next parked break. Nothing is added to the row.

title: The Timer Starts Before Anyone Chooses a Finish
premise: A traveler starts a short timer during a parked pause, then leaves it out of frame before it reaches the end. Later, the same timer is restarted without explaining what it was meant to count.

title: One Date Gets Two Identical Check Marks
premise: A traveler checks a date on a plain daily chart, then marks the same box again during a later break. The two marks sit together without a note about what either one records.

title: One Tick Mark for Every Waiting Morning at Pigeon Gorge
premise: Stuck at the I-40 Pigeon River Gorge washout, a traveler makes one tick mark on a card for every morning the crossing stays closed. The odometer doesn't move. The tick marks do.

title: The Clock Goes Back, the Day Keeps Its Place
premise: Crossing a time zone, the traveler sets the dashboard clock back while the day's to-do list stays in the order things actually happened. The car gains an hour, and nobody can find anything to do with it.

title: A Calendar Mark for a Wait Is Not a Day Off
premise: A traveler marks the calendar two ways: a circle for a rest day they chose, an X for a day the road made them wait. The X's are winning.

title: A Routine With No Appointment Hour Still Holds the Day
premise: A traveler starts the trip with a chart that gives every task an exact hour, and the delays turn it into a grid of crossed-out promises. They redraw it as a plain list of things to do whenever there's a pause, and something on it finally gets finished.
